lesson_title: The Food of the Future - Today

slides.title: THE FOOD OF THE FUTURE - TODAY
slides.subtitle: How do we choose what we eat?

items.text: SCAN THE FEED FOR FUTURE FOODS

strategy_items.text: Look at the statements. Do they sound like science or science-fiction?
Consult your partner. Use your background knowledge!

slides.title: FACT OR FICTION?
slides.rationale: Activate your background knowledge about unusual future foods.
slides.content:
STATEMENTVERDICT
1. Future burgers will be made of 100% bugs.FACT (Insect protein)
2. You can grow a steak in a laboratory.FACT (Cultured meat)
3. Digital food can be tasted through a screen.FICTION (Not yet!)

strategy_items.text: Context is King: Read the whole sentence, not just the word.
Visual Proof: Every image on the screen is a clue to the definition.
Morphology: Look for prefixes like 'un-' to flip the meaning.

slides.context_sentence: Japanese food uses sea plants – algae and others.
slides.notes: Algae: simple non-flowering plants of a large group that includes the seaweeds.

slides.context_sentence: To be honest, the flavor is unexceptional for a snack bar – you know, nothing special.
slides.notes: Unexceptional: not out of the ordinary; ordinary.

slides.context_sentence: The crickets are made into flour. You can buy the flour online.
slides.notes: Crickets: leaping insects related to the grasshoppers.

slides.context_sentence: Everything is made up of molecules – tiny pieces of chemicals.
slides.notes: Molecules: the smallest physical unit of an element or compound.

slides.context_sentence: They extract heme from plants, and put it into their food product.
slides.notes: Extract: to remove or take out, especially by effort or force.

strategy_items.text: Don't read for meaning yet! Look for keywords and layout features.
Your eyes should 'bounce' across the page.

slides.title: SCAN THE FEED
slides.text: SCAN THE FEED! Which 3 future foods are discussed?

strategy_items.text: Is it a Noun (thing), Verb (action), or Adjective (description)?
Find synonyms in the text to confirm your guess.

slides.title: VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT
slides.content:
WORDPART OF SPEECHCLUE / MEANING
1. algaeNounSea plants (synonym)
2. unexceptionalAdjective'un-' = not / Nothing special
3. cricketsNounInsects (explanation)
4. extractVerb'Put into' (opposite)

strategy_items.text: 'I think it's true' isn't enough. Find the exact sentence!
If it's FALSE, what is the correct information?

slides.title: FACT OR FICTION?
slides.content:
STATEMENTVERDICT
1. Typical Japanese dish?FALSE
2. Juice makes them unexceptional?FALSE
3. Cricket flour has protein?TRUE
4. Heme from real beef?FALSE

slides.question: The food in the photo is a typical Japanese dish.
slides.evidence: [Para 1] "I know Japanese food... uses sea plants – algae and others. But this is the first time I've used it in a snack bar recipe!"
slides.explanation: Algae is Japanese, but the snack bar is a new invention.

slides.question: Using orange juice makes the bars unexceptional.
slides.evidence: [Para 3] "the sweetener is orange juice! ... To be honest, the flavor is unexceptional for a snack bar."
slides.explanation: The flavor is unexceptional (ordinary), but the orange juice is just the sweetener.

slides.question: Cricket flour contains a lot of protein.
slides.evidence: [Para 6] "Apparently insects are also a great source of protein... The crickets are made into flour."
slides.explanation: The text confirms insects (crickets) are a 'perfect protein'.

slides.question: Heme for artificial beef is extracted from real beef.
slides.evidence: [Para 8] "They extract heme from plants, and put it into their food product..."
slides.explanation: Heme is found in all living things, and they extract it from plants for the burger.

strategy_items.text: Quote specific environmental or taste data from the social feed.

slides.title: THE FINAL VERDICT
slides.content:
QUESTIONANSWER
1. Better for environment?YES
2. Evidence it tastes like beef?YES

slides.question: Is growing algae better for the environment than traditional farming?
slides.evidence: [Para 5] "Traditional farming has a big carbon footprint. Algae doesn't. Also it's very easy to grow, and doesn't use a lot of fresh water."
slides.explanation: Algae has a lower carbon footprint and uses less fresh water.

slides.question: Is there any evidence that The Impossible Burger tastes like 'real' beef?
slides.evidence: [Para 15] "But I've seen online videos of people who have tried it, and they say it tastes just like real beef!"
slides.explanation: The speaker cites video evidence of people's reactions.

strategy_items.text: Which food wins the 'Gold Badge' of the future?

slides.title: YOUR PREFERENCES
slides.content: Which would you eat? Why?

slides.title: FUTURE FOOD REVIEW
slides.text:
Write your 40-60 word review.
Mention Flavor, Texture, and the Planet.

slides.question: Review Model
slides.evidence: [Para 1] "I just tried the algae snack bar! The nutty flavor is unexceptional but the texture is great. Plus, it's better for the planet than traditional snacks!"
slides.explanation: A concise social media review hitting all criteria.
